title: The Parser Monad: pure, bind, map, then, and skip
description: Wrap parser functions in a Parser class with pure and bind so sequencing, mapping, and skipping can be chained like monadic do-notation.

steps.description: Define the Parser class with pure(cls, value) returning (value, pos) without consuming input, and bind(self, f) running self(s, pos) and passing val into f(val)(s, pos2).
Implement map, then, and skip directly in terms of bind and Parser.pure.

steps.question: What is the difference between p.then(other) on line 29 and p.skip(other) on line 33?
steps.answer: Both run p first and then other, but p.then(other) discards p's value and returns other's value, while p.skip(other) keeps p's value v and discards other's value.

steps.description: Wrap char_p, regex_p, and lit_p as Parser instances, and build tok(p) = p.skip(ws) to create number and plus.
Chain number.bind(lambda left: plus.then(number).map(lambda right: left + right)) into sum_parser and test it on '3 + 4' and '3 - 4'.
Watch bind pass a parsed value val into f(val)(s, pos2) at the updated input position pos2.
